messages.subject: space-time continuous model in INLA
parts:
Hi inla group,

I read your SPDE book. In Section 7.2, you introduce space-time continuous models which use knots and define a temporal mesh.
However, could you please tell me that what is the model specification (mathmatically)? It looks very different to space-time discrete model, eg. Cameletti Case.

Many thanks
Charles

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] space-time continuous model in INLA
parts:
Hi,

In Section 7.2, the model is almost the same as in Cameletti et al; an
AR(1) process in time on the temporal basis functions, kronecker with
a 2D SPDE in space.
The difference is that in Cameletti et al, the knots were integers
equal to the timepoints. In 7.2 and 7.3of the book, other knot
placements are used. The knot choice in 7.2 actually does looks a bit
odd, but perhaps it makes sense when comparing to the time values of
the data. In 7.3., fewer knots than data timepoints are used, to
reduce the model resolution and therefore reduce the computational
cost.

Finn
